One of the best incrementals I've ever played, with a massive focus on active play. It's one of those games that you can take a year to beat your first run if you're idling, but around two-three weeks if you're actively playing. Absolutely massive game with a lot of fun little changes of pace in the form of respec mechanics that get more and more interesting the more you play.

For players more familiar with the myriad of modern incremental/clicker games, Antimatter Dimensions feels oddly spartan and ascetic.

There are no elaborate animations demonstrating one's antimatter production exploding across the screen. No flashy 3D representations of one's exponentially high numerical values. No sprawling, upgrade tree graphically representing by endless branching options. Just numbers, buttons, menus, and the quiet satisfaction of watching those numbers get progressively more absurd.

Antimatter Dimensions feels like an OG incremental game that never got the memo about how visually elaborate the genre has become and focused primarily upon the mechanics of the game. Said mechanics are stripped down to their bare essentials: purchase upgrades, harvest antimatter, increase production, prestige, unlock new systems, repeat. I had heard reviews before playing talking about how great this game is and admittedly was a little skeptical to try, but I can honestly say this is one of the most fun idle games I've ever played. There's a perfect mix of strategy, trial and error, and delayed progression that keeps you hooked even when things seem frustrating or you hit a wall. The Discord and online communities were super helpful in helping to understand late-game mechanics and of course, numbers go up is super satisfying.

I've been looking for an idle game now that I've beaten this one twice through but have yet to find anything that comes close. Give this one a try you won't regret it! (Also buy a coin pack or two from the shop to support the dev, hopefully they'll create another game someday!)

As idle games go, it's pretty boring.  Better than some I've seen (runs clean, no noticed bugs), but really there's not really any point to it (yes, I know it's an idle game).  Some idle games have a little something extra going for it, something to spice things up.  This one doesn't.  The attempts at humor are not worth the stop, they're more like filler text and something to make the tedium of the whole endeavor seem more palatable.  If all you care about are high numbers, a tedious litany of hoops to jump through challenges and achievements, sure, go for it.  But that's about all this one has going for it, if you're into that.  It's clear some folks like it, but I wouldn't recommend it unless it's specifically your thing.

reviews.title: happy enough to have this game again to cry
reviews.text:
i have loved AD for YEARS, to the point that i ended up saving the original github page as a shortcut on my phone, as that was as close as i could get to having it as an app since Apple didn’t want to let it onto the app store. you have NO IDEA how freaking happy i am to finally have it again—it’s actually the reason i got into incremental games, and i’d just so happened to have searched “incremental games” again and saw my beloved Antimatter Dimensions TvT i clicked download faster than i ever have before, i don’t care that i don’t have either of my previous saves anymore, i’ll start this game over from scratch however many times i need to, but now i won’t have to ever again!
thank you SO MUCH for bringing this to the app store!! this is the ONE idle-incremental prestige game (and the only one for all those categories) that i’ve ever recommended anyone to play!

reviews.title: Quite literally the best of a genre
reviews.text: I’ve tried so many idle/incremental games and this one stands out. Don’t let the minimal design dissuade you, the way progress is handled has enough life and content to make up for it. My absolute favorite thing about this game is the way it hides the direction it’s going and the sheer scale that direction is achieving. For any fan of the genre, this is an absolute must play.

reviews.title: The greatest incremental game ever
reviews.text: Unfortunately this game is so good, I played it on PC for like, a few months, I think it took me 2-3 months to beat the entire game and it was a perfectly paced experience with incredible depth and difficulty and now I can’t enjoy most incremental games because this game was so perfect. Please god play it if you can, but be warned all other incremental games with pale in comparison

reviews.title: Android’s First iOS Game
reviews.text:
Looks like the Android app — if you’re coming from that device you’ll feel right at home. But on iOS it misses the mark. Looks dated. Is that Material design? Ignores my notch. Triggers Siri at the bottom of the phone. Do you love opening an app and seeing buttons, then you have buttons! Wondering what you should do in this monstrosity of information overload? Me too. 

Absolute amateur hour that doesn’t give the genius of the original AD game any justice. 

Hard pass
